sentences.text:
Sadhna vs National Insurance Company Limited on 6 April, 2026
 Neutral Citation No. 2026:Mphc-Ind:8912
 1 
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh

At Indore
 Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Binod Kumar Dwivedi

On The 6 th Of April, 2026
 Misc. Appeal No. 4406 of 2023
 Sadhna And Others
 Versus
 National Insurance Company Limited And Others
 Appearance:
 Shri Sameer Verma - Advocate for the appellants.

Ms. Priti Keshwani - Advocate for the respondent no.1
 Order

This Misc. Appeal under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been filed by the appellants assailing the impugned award dated 09.05.2023 passed by IV Member, Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Indore (M.P.) in Claim Case No.1846/2021, whereby survivors of deceased Anil Bhoyar have been awarded an amount of Rs.73,89,802/- along with interest.
2.

Learned counsel for the appellants submits that the income has been wrongly assessed even though it has been assessed by the Claims Tribunal on the income tax return which have been filed during the evidence, but average income of three years has been taken, whereas it should have been taken by the last income tax return in the year of accident and if it is done then yearly income would be Rs.6,05,186/-.
For this he has referred to para 27 of the impugned award.
No other dispute has been raised.
On this submission prays for allowing the appeal.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8912 2 MA-4406-2023 3.
Per contra, learned counsel for the Insurance Company has opposed the prayer.

4. Heard and considered the rival submissions raised at bar by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
5.

As far as the income of the deceased is concerned, in the last income tax return, Ex.P-27 that is relating to the year in which the accident took place, the income of the deceased has been given as Rs.6,05,186/-
Therefore, the Claims Tribunal has wrongly taken the average of the income of the deceased on the basis of the income tax return of three years.
Thus, the income of the deceased be taken as Rs.6,05,186/-.
Other points are not in dispute.

Accordingly, the just and proper Sadhna vs National Insurance Company Limited on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/190188882/
1 compensation comes as under:-
Loss of Rs.6,05,186/-(income as ITR) +25% FP less 1/4 Dependency (personal expenses) x 13 =Rs.73,75,706/-
